function.name: get_boiling_melting_points
function.description: Retrieve the boiling point and melting point of a substance based on its name and the sea level. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Wait "海平面下5000米處" could mean at 5000 meters below sea level (i.e., undersea depth). But typical phrase "海平面上" means above sea level. "海平面下" means below sea level. So they want boiling point and melting point of water at 5000 meters below sea level. That is deep ocean. Pressure increases with depth. At 5000 m depth, pressure ~ 50 atm? Actually pressure increases about 1 atm per 10 m depth. So at 5000 m, pressure ~ 500 atm. Boiling point increases with pressure. But water's boiling point at high pressure can be above 100°C. But at 500 atm, water's boiling point is around 300°C? Let's approximate. But we need to use the function get_boiling_melting_points. The function expects "substance" and "sea_level" in meters. But "sea_level" is the sea level in meters? Actually the function description: "Retrieve the boiling point and melting point of a substance based on its name and the sea level." It says "sea level in meters". That seems odd: sea level is usually 0 m. Maybe they mean "altitude"? But the function signature: get_boiling_melting_points(substance: string, sea_level: number). So we pass "water" and 5000? But the function expects sea level in meters. If we pass 5000, it might interpret as altitude above sea level. But the user wants below sea level. We could pass -5000? But the function expects number. Could pass -5000. But the function might not handle negative. But we can try.
